title: Lumen: Route + Model Telemetry Slices — immersive dashboard prototype and chart specs
creator: Maya Patel
description: Design an integrated per-route and per-model telemetry "Lumen" dashboard that surfaces latency, throughput, and token metrics as compact interactive slices. Goal: give engineers fast signal-to-action for regressions and cost hotspots without leaving the Console. Deliverables: hi-fi Figma prototype, chart specification doc with aggregation rules, and interaction handoff for front-end engineers.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype includes three primary slices for each route: Latency Distribution, Throughput Timeline, Token Composition; each slice supports 1m/5m/1h rollups.
Latency Distribution shows P50/P90/P99 lines plus an optional violin for distribution on hover and supports SLO ribbon overlay.
Throughput Timeline supports stacked breakdown by model variant and option to overlay cost-per-token as a secondary axis.
Token Composition is a stacked-area view with streaming vs cached token breakdown and per-token cost overlay available.
Interactions: brush-to-zoom across slices, click-to-drill into a specific model version, and quick-create rollout from route header.
Design tokens, spacing, and color palette align with Console design system; annotations and microcopy provided for engineering handoff.
Engineering has all chart props and backend rollup requirements documented; prototype reviewed and signed off by ENG and PM.
Performance: default 1m rollup renders under 250ms in staging when dataset size simulates 10k req/min.
Accessibility: keyboard focus states and tooltips implemented per Console a11y checklist.
QA checklist created with sample queries and expected outputs for each chart type.
comments: 2025-01-29 Maya Patel: Initial draft of the concept after kickoff with PM and SRE. Focused on compactness: three horizontally stacked 'slices' per route row to allow high-density overviews.

2025-02-02 Jonah Rivera: Added interaction flows for brush-to-zoom and cross-slice time sync. Flagged potential performance risk for client-side violin rendering — recommended server-side pre-aggregation for percentiles.
2025-02-04 Priya Singh (PM): Reviewed and prioritised 'quick-create rollout' CTA in the route header. Request: make canary targets accessible from the chart context menu.

2025-02-06 Ravi Kumar (SERVING Eng): Suggestion: default percentiles at P50/P90/P99, but surface P75 as optional to help intermediate anomalies. Backend will expose precomputed quantiles at 1m and 5m windows (ENG-6220).

2025-02-08 Evelyn Cho (Design Lead): Visual critique — violin at full-size is noisy in dense lists; propose showing mini-sparkline violin collapsed and an expanded violin modal on click. Also recommend muted color for cached-token area.
2025-02-10 Jonah Rivera: Implemented chart spec draft and posted GitHub front-end PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/2145; includes Protobuf for rollup metadata and client props.
2025-02-11 QA note (Samir Patel): Verified hover tooltips contain raw counts + percentiles; requested that SLO ribbon include both absolute and relative (percentage) breach annotations.
2025-02-12 Maya Patel: Incorporated feedback, updated Figma, and pushing for ENG review meeting on 2025-02-14 to finalize backend rollup schema. Marking ticket In Review.
Follow-ups: add small-screen behavior and collapse rules, add a migration plan for existing per-route dashboard to Lumen layout.
decisions: Prefer quantile-line overlay (P50,P90,P99) by default; violin is optional and accessible via click — trade-off: readability vs distribution fidelity.
Default aggregation windows: 1m, 5m, 1h. Rationale: 1m for Ops troubleshooting, 1h for trend analysis; 5m balances cost and resolution.
SLO ribbons show absolute threshold with 3-state color band (healthy/warning/breach) and display percent-over-threshold as small badges.
Throughput timeline uses stacked area by model variant, with an optional cost-per-token dashed line on secondary axis; cost computation is server-provided to avoid client drift.
Token Composition distinguishes cached tokens (muted blue) from generated tokens (accent teal) to help diagnose caching regressions quickly.
Microtrace integration: clicking a high-P99 spike opens microtrace quicklist filtered to that time range (backend pointer: ENG-7092).
Performance: precompute percentiles and token-cost aggregates at rollup time; client computes sparklines and micro-interactions only.
Mobile: collapse slices into a stacked vertical flow with a priority-order of Latency > Throughput > Token Composition.
Accessibility: tooltips expose raw numeric values and chart elements are reachable via keyboard shortcuts (next-slice / prev-slice).
notes_for_engineering: Backend should expose precomputed aggregates: count, sum_tokens, p50, p75, p90, p99, violin_buckets for 1m and 5m windows.
API to include 'cache_hit_ratio' per-rollup to render cached-token area accurately.
Include a rollup 'version' field so Console can gracefully handle schema migrations.
Telemetry sampling strategy: 1:1 for 1m window for first 2 weeks of rollout, then adaptive sampling to maintain storage budgets.
Frontend props: chartId, timeRange, rollupWindow, quantiles[], showViolin(boolean), showCostOverlay(boolean).
